title: fix(codex): recover final answers after checkpointed work and terminal reasoning
body:
Closes #185286

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Codex losing its final answer after completed checkpointed work is followed by terminal aggregate reasoning and an empty final response.

## User Impact

The existing passive finalizer can recover the completed result without repeating actions. Strict transcript identity, payload and ordering checks remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing aggregate reasoning block after checkpointed visible work and before the final assistant, matching canonical history. No new prompt, verifier exception, recovery policy, storage field or permission change.

Thanks to @ericcaiwx-star for the fix and regression coverage.

## Evidence

[Built native Gateway capture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185310#issuecomment-6433406222).

Built Linux Gateway and actual pinned Codex app-server 0.164.0, with a local Responses fixture and model confirmed in both real catalogs. Shipped sessions.create plus agent CLI executes a real native command once, then receives terminal aggregate reasoning without a final answer.

Main fails recovery twice with provenance rejection and no finalizer request. This head recovers twice: two source requests, one passive finalizer request containing completed command evidence, CLI exit 0, and the recovered answer in two independent chat.history reads. Every command writes completed-once exactly once; zero tool failures. The finalizer performs no tool calls. A normal-order control recovers on both refs without repeating the command.

Both runtime builds, all 10 native finalizer tests and changed-file formatting/lint passed. Simplification retains the existing blocks and owners: production +8/-8, tests/support +22/-2. No hosted provider acceptance claim.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: revert fully restores old snapshot ordering; no migration or persisted-data rewrite. Blast radius is terminal Codex snapshot ordering after checkpointed work, not model routing, prompts, action authorization or verifier strictness.
